notes: All modules: captures stay in memory or the no-backup cache and are deleted after upload; the session token is never written to storage; the scan fails a write outside its reviewed list.

All modules: no personal data in logcat or exception messages (scans over every module of SdkModule.ALL); no shipped manifest sets backup rules; JMRTD's loggers are silenced and ONNX Runtime telemetry is absent (OrtTelemetryDeviceTest passed in the device suites 22 of 22 on a Pixel 9 (Android 17) at d6af3cc37, twice at the 11A close and once at the 11C close (docs/PROGRESS.md); its emulator leg is a device proof still open).

openverify-sdk: the only cryptography is SHA-256 over consent texts (its own implementation, tested against vectors) and the platform's TLS; nothing is encrypted on the device because nothing is stored.
Not applicable because no module generates, stores or uses a cryptographic key: the session credential is a server token held in memory, and chip keys are derived inside JMRTD for one read.
openverify-sdk: the host's backend creates the inquiry and hands the SDK a session token or one-time link; every decision is the server's, and the SDK decides nothing locally.
Not applicable because the SDK offers no local authentication (no biometric unlock or PIN); the selfie step is evidence sent to the server, not a local factor.
Not applicable because the SDK performs no sensitive operation of its own: each step is authorised by the server per session; any additional factor belongs to the host app.
openverify-sdk: TLS through the platform trust store; plain http only to loopback in a debuggable build; no module sets cleartext traffic, a network security configuration or a custom trust manager.

Pinning is the host app's, through the transport recipe (an OkHttp CertificatePinner with a backup pin), proved by a host test; the SDK ships no pins by design, because each self-hoster has its own certificates (C256.2, decision 41).

All modules: no exported component, provider, receiver or service in any shipped manifest; the SDK's activity is unexported and launched by the host; NFC uses foreground dispatch in the resumed activity.
All modules: no WebView; the scan refuses one in shipped sources (Compose only).
openverify-sdk: FLAG_SECURE on every SDK window (screenshots and the recents view), overlay protections on every screen (HIDE_OVERLAY_WINDOWS).
minSdk 26, targetSdk and compileSdk 36; the host app's own targetSdk governs the platform protections it gets. The release matrix (API 26, 34, 35 with 16 KB pages) has never run (KP10-59).
The SDK declares the flow-spec versions it renders and shows the unsupported screen for a flow it cannot render; forcing an app update is the host app's.

All modules: dependency locking and SHA-256 verification, osv-scanner over the lockfiles in supply-chain.sh, CycloneDX SBOMs of the three AARs (188, 195 and 190 components, cyclonedxBom run locally at the 11C and 11D closes); SCUBA's two files and Eigen are recorded owner exceptions (THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md section 6).

openverify-sdk: server answers are decoded against the contract fixtures and the flow-spec member list; an unknown step or member renders the unsupported screen; chip data is verified on the server (B11-T3).

openverify-sdk: emulator, root and hooking indicators are beta signals, never decisive alone; Play Integrity verdicts only through the host's IntegrityTokenProvider (Phase 10 P3 declined). IntegrityProbesDeviceTest passed in the device suites 22 of 22 on a Pixel 9 (Android 17) at d6af3cc37, twice at the 11A close and once at the 11C close (docs/PROGRESS.md); its emulator leg is a device proof still open.
No module checks its own integrity; the server-side play-integrity provider can judge the app's integrity verdict when the host supplies tokens. The server never trusts the device (B11-T1).

The host app's R8 minifies the SDK with no keep rule for it, since the SDK ships no consumer rule (Workflow 11F, KP10-56); check-consumer-rules.py checks R8's merged configuration. The SDK adds no obfuscation of its own, and nothing in it is a secret.
openverify-sdk: debugger and hooking facts are collected after consent as beta signals for review; nothing blocks dynamic analysis, by design.

All modules: nothing is collected before consent; the signal contract lists each device fact the SDK reads and the scan fails any other read; the permissions are the camera, NFC, network access and hiding other apps' overlays.
Device facts are stored as HMACs under per-environment subkeys on the server, so they link nothing across environments (B7-I4).
The consent texts and the privacy page say what is collected and why; the Google Play Data safety categories are the owner's open item (KP10-61).
A share consent can be withdrawn from the SDK while the flow lives; access, deletion and other rights go through the operator (the subject has no account), as the compliance guide says.
